title: PrintMarshal application integration audit and gap register

scope.authorized_work: Read-only application audit and public integration research; findings written only under research/.
scope.method: Static source inspection, producer-to-consumer path tracing, configuration/schema/test review, and official standards/vendor documentation research.
not_performed: Executing tests/builds or dependency vulnerability scans
Live IdP, SIEM, SMTP or webhook qualification
Account provisioning, sending notifications or deploying connectors
scope.qualification: Absent means not found in the inspected implementation; a type, setting, schema, UI declaration or external protocol does not establish working integration.
assumptions: Single-organization self-hosted installation is the baseline; multi-site is optional.
SaaS services, identity brokers, collectors, message buses and external secret stores must remain optional.
Future device writes require exact driver capability, resource authorization, approvals and recorded results.

priority_definitions.P1: Fix or design before enterprise access or reliance on the affected integration; a delivery priority, not a CVSS severity.
priority_definitions.P2: Core enterprise expansion once its foundations are ready.
priority_definitions.P3: Conditional extension requiring demonstrated customer demand.

effort_definitions.M: A contained connector or cross-cutting improvement with several code paths and operational tests.
effort_definitions.L: A substantial feature spanning persistence, policy, APIs and failure handling.
effort_definitions.XL: A distributed architecture change; requires separate design and qualification.
effort_definitions.note: Relative sizing only; not person-days, a schedule or implementation commitment. Dependencies describe the production-ready design, not prerequisites to fixing a small existing defect.

audit_findings.title: Notification delivery is not durable
audit_findings.observation: Notify launches a goroutine per destination, attempts delivery once, then writes a best-effort notification log. HTTP failures, rate limits and process restarts do not lead to persisted retry.
audit_findings.impact: SIEM, incident and email events can disappear while the underlying fleet operation succeeds; burst fan-out has no bounded delivery worker.
audit_findings.recommendation: Commit an event/outbox record durably; add bounded workers, destination leases, retry classification, Retry-After, dead letters and replay using stable event IDs.

audit_findings.title: Declared and delivered event sets differ
audit_findings.observation: Notifier configuration names job.finished, but the job runner emits job.updated only to the Hub. Manual alert clear/ack and consumable replacement events also publish to the Hub without the notifier.
audit_findings.impact: An incident can remain open externally after an operator clears it, and subscribers can configure an event that is never delivered.
audit_findings.recommendation: Define a single event catalogue and route all eligible transitions through the durable publisher; record automatic versus manual resolution and preserve event origin.

audit_findings.title: Audit records can be silently lost and omit security context
audit_findings.observation: The API audit helper discards AddAudit errors. Login/logout and middleware denials do not create audit events. Audit rows lack request ID, immutable principal ID, origin IP, principal type and external export state.
audit_findings.impact: A security team cannot reliably reconstruct access and actions or assume that every recorded change has an audit trail.
audit_findings.recommendation: Make local mutations and audit/outbox atomic; persist intent and outcome separately for future printer I/O; record authentication/denial events with bounded redacted context.

audit_findings.title: Password changes preserve old sessions and mint an extra session
audit_findings.observation: changePassword calls Login to verify the current password, causing an additional persisted session whose token is discarded. SetPassword updates only password_hash and does not invalidate other sessions.
audit_findings.impact: Changing a compromised password does not terminate a stolen bearer session; unused sessions accumulate until expiry or deletion.
audit_findings.recommendation: Separate password verification from session issuance; invalidate or rotate sessions according to explicit policy after password/identity changes and expose administrator revocation.

audit_findings.title: Live streams outlive authorization and accept broad origins
audit_findings.observation: WebSocket authentication occurs at handshake. ServeHTTP allows wildcard origins and never rechecks session expiry or user revocation. TokenFromRequest accepts access_token query parameters for every API request, not just WebSockets.
audit_findings.impact: A previously authorized stream can continue after logout/deletion/expiry; query tokens can leak through infrastructure URL logging. This is not an unauthenticated WebSocket bypass: authentication and SameSiteStrict cookies still exist.
audit_findings.recommendation: Restrict origins, remove long-lived query tokens, enforce stream revocation/expiry, and later filter events by resource scope.

audit_findings.title: Enterprise transport and device trust are not configured by default
audit_findings.observation: The server calls ListenAndServe with HTTP; secure cookies default false, and deployment exposes the host-network listener. IPP defaults prefer clear HTTP and enable InsecureSkipVerify for HTTPS reads.
audit_findings.impact: Credentials require a separately secured ingress; printer identity is not cryptographically verified by default. Read-only polling limits device mutation but does not establish trustworthy telemetry.
audit_findings.recommendation: Document a tested TLS ingress profile and trusted proxy rules; enable secure cookies; add per-connector/device CA bundles or pins and explicit discovery-only trust exceptions.

audit_findings.title: SMTP ignores the notification deadline
audit_findings.observation: Notify creates a 20-second context, but sendMail does not accept it and calls smtp.Dial with no application connection/read/write deadline.
audit_findings.impact: Unresponsive SMTP servers can retain goroutines beyond the intended timeout and make shutdown/delivery health unreliable.
audit_findings.recommendation: Use context-aware dialing and per-phase socket deadlines, bounded email workers, validated headers and explicit TLS modes.

audit_findings.title: SMTP authentication has no modern provider route
audit_findings.observation: Only smtp.PlainAuth is implemented. There is no XOAUTH2 token acquisition, Graph sendMail or connector credential lifecycle.
audit_findings.impact: Modern Microsoft 365 policies and other OAuth-only deployments cannot use this path directly; it still works with a compatible local relay.
audit_findings.recommendation: Keep local SMTP/relay support and add OAuth SMTP or scoped Graph sending. Treat provider acceptance separately from mailbox delivery.

audit_findings.title: Teams compatibility needs a Workflows migration contract
audit_findings.observation: The Teams formatter posts a MessageCard with no configurable HTTP authorization header or documented Workflow authentication/ownership setup.
audit_findings.impact: Old Office 365 Connector URLs are retired. MessageCard itself is not universally invalid: current Workflows supports rendering it, with limitations.
audit_findings.recommendation: Document and test Workflows endpoints, authentication and supported card schemas; use Adaptive Cards for interactive flows and handle expired endpoints/owner changes.

audit_findings.title: Authentication and machine identity are local-only
audit_findings.observation: Auth supports local bcrypt users and opaque sessions. There are no OIDC/SAML/SCIM routes, identity-provider mappings, MFA assurance handling or first-class scoped service accounts.
audit_findings.impact: Enterprise lifecycle, conditional access and automation must rely on separately managed local users or human sessions.
audit_findings.recommendation: Implement generic OIDC and separate service principals first; use a broker for SAML/LDAP where suitable; retain controlled local recovery access; add SCIM for lifecycle.

audit_findings.title: Authorization is global and coarse
audit_findings.observation: Role.Allows is a three-level rank. require only checks that rank. Existing groups and credential scopes route fleet work but do not constrain which resources a user can read or change.
audit_findings.impact: A site operator or integration cannot be limited to a site/group/action; global streams and exports share that boundary.
audit_findings.recommendation: Add action/resource policy checks across list, single-object, export, bulk jobs, streams and credentials. Separate security/firmware permissions and approval roles before writes ship.

audit_findings.title: SIEM export and printer-log ingestion are absent
audit_findings.observation: There is no SIEM exporter, syslog receiver, OTLP receiver/exporter or normalized device-security log store. The security.syslog.server catalogue entry describes a future printer setting, not a running receiver.
audit_findings.impact: Application audit export, printer security collection and operational telemetry cannot be treated as existing end-to-end integrations.
audit_findings.recommendation: Implement separate pipelines with common identity/correlation; support a qualified external collector before building a general log-storage product.

audit_findings.title: Trap attribution and storm controls are incomplete
audit_findings.observation: The listener uses gosnmp.Default, clears the community restriction and matches devices by source IP. No application SNMPv3 trap-user configuration or rate/coalescing policy is visible. A matched trap can raise an alert and submit a poll.
audit_findings.impact: Spoofed or burst events on reachable networks can contaminate evidence and induce extra poll/notification work; SNMP polling v3 support does not prove authenticated trap reception.
audit_findings.recommendation: Provide source policies, configured v3 security where supported, trust labels, bounded input/rate limits and coalesced reconciliation; never execute remediation based only on an untrusted log/trap.

audit_findings.title: Integration secrets lack managed rotation and references
audit_findings.observation: Device secrets use AES-GCM and a single operator-supplied or generated key. Webhook URLs are config-file values; SMTP references an environment variable. There is no connector secret reference abstraction or key version/rotation workflow.
audit_findings.impact: Webhook URLs themselves are bearer secrets; enterprise secret stores and key rotation cannot be connected consistently.
audit_findings.recommendation: Add secretRef resolution with minimum privileges, versioned key handling and rotation tests; support mounted files first and optional Vault/managed secret backends.

audit_findings.title: REST export is not a stable incremental sync contract
audit_findings.observation: Routes are unversioned and deviceFilter has no updated-since cursor. listDevices reports total as len(returned devices), including when a limit applies. No OpenAPI contract, idempotency-key flow or dedicated integration API credentials were found.
audit_findings.impact: CMDB/ITSM automation needs custom polling and can misinterpret a page count as a collection total or duplicate actions after retries.
audit_findings.recommendation: Publish a versioned OpenAPI contract with accurate pagination, cursors/tombstones, external IDs, conflict rules, request IDs and idempotent command submission.

audit_findings.title: Application health has little external instrumentation
audit_findings.observation: JSON slog is optional, HTTP access logging is debug-level, and /healthz returns a static OK/version response. No Prometheus endpoint or OpenTelemetry instrumentation was found.
audit_findings.impact: Operators cannot see delivery backlog age, failed exports, DB readiness, scheduler lag or stale fleet data using their existing observability stack.
audit_findings.recommendation: Add readiness and metrics first, then OTLP correlation. Keep device telemetry/metrics distinct from immutable audit delivery and constrain label cardinality.

audit_findings.title: PKI/configuration/firmware interfaces are scaffolding
audit_findings.observation: SCEP/EST/ACME enums and CAProfile exist, but the three feature route files are empty, service facades do not implement the workflows, and vendor plugin registration is empty.
audit_findings.impact: Certificate enrollment, policy-remediation or signed firmware integrations cannot be advertised based on type names or schemas.
audit_findings.recommendation: Build CA-provider and printer-install adapters with separate compatibility records, and place all device writes behind capability, approval and audit controls.

audit_findings.title: Generated bootstrap password is written into ordinary logs
audit_findings.observation: When no initial password is provided, Bootstrap logs the generated password in a warning event on the application's normal logger.
audit_findings.impact: Shipping stdout wholesale to a SIEM can copy the initial administrator credential into a broader-access log system.
audit_findings.recommendation: Use a protected bootstrap handoff or supply the existing environment setting; explicitly prevent bootstrap secret fields from reaching centralized logs and verify redaction.

integration_gaps.title: Generic OIDC single sign-on
integration_gaps.proposal: Server-side authorization code flow with PKCE, issuer discovery/JWKS validation, stable issuer+subject identity, explicit group-to-role/scope mapping and a protected local recovery account.
acceptance_criteria: Reject wrong issuer/audience/signature/nonce and replayed codes.
Exercise key rotation, IdP outage, group removal and two users whose email is reused.
Use IdP MFA/assurance policy without treating an ID token as a general API access token.

integration_gaps.title: SCIM provisioning and deprovisioning
integration_gaps.proposal: Provision Users/Groups and deactivate accounts through SCIM 2.0 with bounded filtering, external IDs and explicit ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Deactivation revokes HTTP sessions and streams within a documented bound.
Retries do not duplicate users; group removal removes derived permissions.
SCIM provisioning never grants default administrator access.

integration_gaps.title: SAML and LDAP/AD compatibility through a broker
integration_gaps.proposal: Document a supported self-hosted broker configuration for existing SAML and LDAP/AD estates; build native SAML/LDAP only for justified requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Test brokered login, group mapping, offboarding and outage/recovery.
LDAP credentials are confined to the broker and transport is authenticated.
Recovery access remains possible without silently bypassing authorization.

integration_gaps.title: Action and resource-scoped authorization
integration_gaps.proposal: Add principal/action/resource checks and explicit site/group scope; distinguish credential routing from authorization and split future firmware/security privileges.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-site list, direct ID, export, job, telemetry and WebSocket access are denied or filtered consistently.
Bulk targets are authorized at submission and execution; dynamic group edits cannot expand access silently.
Security approval and execution can be assigned to different principals.

integration_gaps.title: Scoped service accounts and API credentials
integration_gaps.proposal: First-class machine principals with expiring, revocable, scoped credentials; use opaque hashed tokens or validated external client-credentials access tokens.
acceptance_criteria: An inventory sync token cannot change stock, credentials or printers.
Rotation and revocation take effect on HTTP and streams; actor identity appears in audit.
Never require a human administrator password for a connector.

integration_gaps.title: Session lifecycle and local authentication hardening
integration_gaps.proposal: Separate verification from issuance, revoke/rotate sessions, eliminate long-lived query tokens, restrict WebSocket origins, add bounded login throttling and identity change hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Password change invalidates selected old sessions and does not mint a discarded session.
Logout, expiry and account disable terminate or invalidate active streams.
Credential stuffing is rate limited without allowing arbitrary account lockout denial of service.

integration_gaps.title: TLS ingress, trusted proxies and per-connector/device trust
integration_gaps.proposal: Tested reverse-proxy/native TLS deployment profiles, secure cookies, public base URL, trusted forwarded headers, outbound CA/mTLS/proxy settings and explicit printer trust modes.
acceptance_criteria: Default enterprise profile never transmits login credentials over clear HTTP.
Forged forwarded headers do not change trusted identity/source attribution.
CA rotation, pin mismatch and scoped self-signed device discovery behave predictably.

integration_gaps.title: Canonical event catalogue and versioned envelope
integration_gaps.proposal: Create stable event IDs and source identity, original/observed timestamps, schema version, actor/resource/job/correlation IDs and explicit lifecycle event types.
acceptance_criteria: Events validate against a published schema.
Retries preserve event ID and original event time; delivery attempts have separate IDs/times.
Every declared event has an identified producer and test.

integration_gaps.title: Durable outbox and bounded connector workers
integration_gaps.proposal: SQLite transaction-backed event/outbox and per-destination delivery state first; add bounded workers, leases, backoff/jitter, Retry-After, dead letters, replay and retention controls.
acceptance_criteria: An event survives a crash after state commit and before network send.
429/5xx/timeouts retry within policy; permanent errors stop with visible reason.
A slow destination does not block polling or other destinations; duplicate delivery is explicitly supported.

integration_gaps.title: Signed authenticated outbound webhooks
integration_gaps.proposal: Versioned payloads, HMAC signature/timestamp, key ID/rotation, configurable authentication and destination policies including approved internal endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: A receiver verifies raw-body integrity and rejects stale/replayed signatures.
Redirections cannot leak credentials or leave approved destination policy.
Requests obey timeouts, size limits, TLS verification and retry rules; log entries redact webhook secrets.

integration_gaps.title: Complete alert/job/stock routing and suppression
integration_gaps.proposal: Centralize all selected transition events and add severity/site filters, deduplication, maintenance windows, escalation, digest and flapping policies.
acceptance_criteria: Automatic and manual clear both update an external incident according to policy.
A configured job.finished subscription receives terminal success/partial/failure consistently.
Acknowledgment is not confused with resolution and routine stock changes cannot flood on-call.

integration_gaps.title: Reliable secure SMTP transport
integration_gaps.proposal: Context/deadline-aware SMTP, explicit STARTTLS/implicit TLS/approved relay modes, safe MIME/header encoding, retry classification and test-send diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: A stalled connect/TLS/DATA operation exits within its configured deadline.
Subjects/addresses containing CR/LF cannot inject headers.
Transient failure is retried and accepted mail is not labelled delivered-to-inbox.

integration_gaps.title: OAuth SMTP and Microsoft Graph mail
integration_gaps.proposal: Provider-auth abstraction; retain local relay and add XOAUTH2 or application-scoped Graph sendMail with refresh/expiry handling and mailbox restrictions.
acceptance_criteria: Send using a tenant that disables password SMTP authentication.
Restrict sending to the intended mailbox and test credential expiry/rotation.
Differentiate provider acceptance, retryable failure and optional delivery feedback.

integration_gaps.title: Microsoft Teams Workflows support
integration_gaps.proposal: Document and test Workflows endpoint/authentication and ownership; support appropriate MessageCard/Adaptive Card payloads and endpoint migration.
acceptance_criteria: A new Workflows endpoint renders a notification in the chosen channel.
Tenant-authenticated flow requirements and owner removal are tested.
Retired connector URLs produce an actionable migration error rather than silent success.

integration_gaps.title: Normalized application security/audit export
integration_gaps.proposal: Separate security/audit export from debug logs; provide canonical JSON/collector handoff and optional RFC5424/TLS output with versioned mappings.
acceptance_criteria: Failed login, denial, credential change and future printer action reach the selected destination with correlation.
No bootstrap/session/device secret is exported.
Delivery acknowledgments and gaps are visible and source event IDs survive conversion.

integration_gaps.title: Splunk HEC adapter or qualified collector path
integration_gaps.proposal: HEC token/auth, endpoint/index/source/sourcetype mapping, batching and response validation; enable indexer acknowledgment only on supported/configured deployments.
acceptance_criteria: HEC envelope is accepted and searchable with event ID and device/principal fields.
Token-disabled, wrong-index, throttling and ambiguous response cases are handled.
Document whether success means accepted or indexer-acknowledged for this Splunk deployment.

integration_gaps.title: Microsoft Sentinel supported ingestion paths
integration_gaps.proposal: Offer Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API with DCR/table/service identity, or a documented syslog/CEF via AMA forwarder; treat them as distinct architectures.
acceptance_criteria: A record arrives in the expected custom/CommonSecurityLog/Syslog table with correct time semantics.
DCR permissions and schema mismatch failures are visible.
Do not configure the same event twice through parallel routes without deduplication.

integration_gaps.title: Elastic/ECS and general log-backend mappings
integration_gaps.proposal: Publish ECS mapping for Elastic Security and a qualified collector handoff for other backends; retain application events distinct from printer-origin logs.
acceptance_criteria: Elastic Security-required fields have valid values rather than raw proprietary JSON alone.
Preserve original/observed timestamps and event identity.
A backend-specific adapter/pipeline is tested before claiming compatibility; OTLP alone is not universal SIEM compatibility.

integration_gaps.title: Printer syslog collection and normalization
integration_gaps.proposal: Use an optional external syslog collector first, feeding an authenticated normalized event intake; support documented printer formats and explicit TLS/legacy UDP trust classes.
acceptance_criteria: Replay captured model/firmware log fixtures for login, setting/certificate changes and reboot events.
Preserve raw evidence reference, timestamps, source transport, parser version and attribution confidence.
Malformed bursts, unknown sources and disk exhaustion cannot starve API/polling; UDP is not advertised as lossless.

integration_gaps.title: Authenticated and rate-controlled SNMP trap intake
integration_gaps.proposal: Configure source policies and v3 USM users where devices support them; bound/coalesce events and keep trap-to-poll reconciliation separate from remediation.
acceptance_criteria: An unknown or untrusted source cannot impersonate an authenticated printer event.
Burst traps coalesce polling and do not create unbounded jobs/notifications.
Boot/time/security failures are handled and transport trust is visible in exported evidence.

integration_gaps.title: Prometheus metrics, readiness and OTLP
integration_gaps.proposal: Application readiness/metrics plus optional OTLP logs/traces, correlation across API/jobs/connectors, and reference dashboards/alerts; expose fleet metrics selectively.
acceptance_criteria: Measure oldest delivery age, dead letters, poll freshness, scheduler lag and integration failures.
Document metric cardinality budgets and endpoint authorization.
An unavailable collector does not block the product; health distinguishes process alive from DB/delivery readiness.

integration_gaps.title: ServiceNow / Jira Service Management incident lifecycle
integration_gaps.proposal: Map alert lifecycle to ticket create/update/resolve with external object IDs, field mappings, suppression, idempotency and loop prevention.
acceptance_criteria: A retry creates one ticket, not duplicates.
Clear and re-open follow a documented lifecycle with evidence links.
Authenticated external changes cannot bypass site/action authorization or initiate printer writes.

integration_gaps.title: PagerDuty Events API v2 lifecycle
integration_gaps.proposal: Trigger/acknowledge/resolve using a stable alert-incarnation dedup key, severity mapping and routing key; keep stock warnings below paging threshold by default.
acceptance_criteria: Raise/ack/clear map correctly and duplicate triggers coalesce.
A re-opened condition uses a deliberate new incarnation or explicit reuse policy.
202 acceptance, 429, 5xx and replay are distinguished; credentials are never logged.

integration_gaps.title: CMDB/asset sync with explicit field ownership
integration_gaps.proposal: ServiceNow IRE, NetBox and Snipe-IT adapters/bridges with external IDs and source-of-truth rules; reconcile using stable device evidence, not IP alone.
acceptance_criteria: An address change does not create a duplicate asset.
Discovered facts update without overwriting operator/CMDB-owned location, owner or asset tag.
Reconciliation dry-run, conflicts, tombstones and offline targets have documented behavior.

integration_gaps.title: Connector secret references and rotation
integration_gaps.proposal: Shared secretRef interface for encrypted local store, mounted files and optional Vault KV; separate webhook/API/SMTP/IdP/CA credentials and version key material.
acceptance_criteria: Rotate a secret without revealing it in UI/log/export and document reload behavior.
Secret backend outage has bounded cache/expiry and failure semantics.
Backup/restore and encryption-key rotation preserve decryptability under explicit access control.

integration_gaps.title: CA enrollment separated from printer certificate deployment
integration_gaps.proposal: CA-provider adapters for enterprise PKI (Vault PKI, SCEP/EST/ACME as justified), plus separate per-device CSR/install/renew drivers and capability evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Issue/sign and device install are separate, audited results.
Prefer on-device private keys when supported; validate chain/SAN/EKU/time and renewal failures.
Renewal does not silently enable unsupported printer-native enrollment or lose the management channel.

integration_gaps.title: Versioned OpenAPI and dependable sync/command API
integration_gaps.proposal: Versioned schema, accurate totals/cursors, external IDs, idempotency keys, request IDs, async job outcome semantics and examples for Ansible/curl before bespoke SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Generated clients validate contract and pagination is stable during changes.
A timeout/retry does not duplicate a command.
Ansible examples verify final job results and do not claim check-mode behavior unsupported by the API/module.

integration_gaps.title: Authenticated inbound callbacks and action requests
integration_gaps.proposal: Versioned authenticated inbound API with replay/dedup protection, issuer/source policy, scoped principals and explicit callback-to-action mapping.
acceptance_criteria: A forged/replayed incident callback cannot ack or mutate an unrelated resource.
Webhook payloads never execute shell commands or bypass printer-operation approvals.
Callback loops are prevented by origin/correlation IDs and authority rules.

integration_gaps.title: Transactional security audit and intent/outcome journal
integration_gaps.proposal: Durable principal/action/outcome events, append restrictions, local transaction coupling and explicit printer I/O intent/outcome records; exports reference immutable source IDs.
acceptance_criteria: Simulated local audit persistence failure cannot silently commit an unaudited privileged metadata change.
A crash/timeout during future printer I/O yields reconcilable pending/unknown outcome, not false success.
Login success/failure, authorization denial, break-glass use and secret rotation are recorded without secret values.

integration_gaps.title: Retention, external archive and restore contract
integration_gaps.proposal: Separate policies for metrics, raw printer logs, audit, attempts and dead letters; optional protected object archive, backups, key recovery and tested restore.
acceptance_criteria: Disk-full policy preserves audit/delivery evidence within the stated acceptance bound.
Retention/restore cannot silently replay resolved incidents or lose dedup state.
WORM/retention settings are validated on the actual storage target; generic S3 compatibility is not proof of Object Lock.

integration_gaps.title: Integration configuration, health and diagnostics UI/API
integration_gaps.proposal: Admin-managed connector records, validation/test-send, redacted previews, per-destination status, delivery history, replay authorization and config audit.
acceptance_criteria: Operators can identify revoked credentials, schema rejection, stale queues and disabled connectors.
Test messages are clearly labelled and never trigger printer actions.
Editing and replay privileges are separate from viewing diagnostics; probe responses cannot expose secrets.

integration_gaps.title: Site collectors and customer network boundaries
integration_gaps.proposal: Optional outbound-connected site collectors with mTLS identities/site scope, local spool, revocation, version negotiation and explicit printer-credential placement.
acceptance_criteria: Same private IP at two sites cannot collide.
Collector compromise is bounded to its site and revocation is effective.
Offline replay preserves original timestamps and site identity without granting remote shell access.

integration_gaps.title: Vendor advisories, NVD and KEV correlation
integration_gaps.proposal: Cached advisory/CPE/KEV enrichment with evidence-backed product and component-firmware mapping, confidence and applicability state.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown or missing firmware is reported as unknown rather than compliant.
Marketing-name similarity alone cannot confirm vulnerability.
Offline feed updates preserve provenance and do not trigger automatic firmware installation.

integration_gaps.title: NAC / Cisco ISE context enrichment
integration_gaps.proposal: Read-only network/identity context through a customer-selected NAC connector; preserve endpoint identity/time and distinguish network quarantine from printer administration.
acceptance_criteria: A stale MAC/IP correlation is marked uncertain.
Connector access is scoped and audited.
No automatic quarantine/change-of-authorization is enabled without a separate designed approval path.

integration_gaps.title: GitOps/configuration import and change-system linkage
integration_gaps.proposal: Validated desired-state imports, external change IDs, preview/diff and approvals once device-write workflows exist; keep secrets as references.
acceptance_criteria: A repository change can be previewed without touching printers.
Only supported settings/capabilities reach a scoped campaign.
Approval and external change IDs remain attached to every final device result.

integration_gaps.title: Ownership/IPAM/site metadata enrichment
integration_gaps.proposal: Customer-owned site/asset/owner metadata imports with provenance, field authority and conflict resolution; identifiers are not permissions.
acceptance_criteria: Operator-owned fields survive rediscovery and sync.
A CMDB tag/group does not independently grant access.
Missing owner/site values do not cause silent reassignment or resource-scope expansion.

integration_gaps.title: Scheduled external reports and evidence exports
integration_gaps.proposal: Scheduled scoped inventory/compliance/stock exports using authenticated download links or approved object storage/email; report actual unknown coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Large exports are paginated/snapshotted and authorized for the service principal.
Links expire and exclude secrets; delivery is audited.
Security reports cannot claim assessments that the current scaffold has not performed.

integration_gaps.title: Read-only MCP/assistant integration
integration_gaps.proposal: An optional read-only adapter over the same scoped API, with separate audience-validated access and untrusted device/log content handling.
acceptance_criteria: Tool calls cannot exceed API resource scope or pass through unrelated bearer tokens.
Printer names/log text cannot authorize actions or alter policy.
Write-capable tools remain deferred until explicit approval and device-operation safeguards exist.

integration_gaps.title: Approved firmware repositories and offline evidence packages
integration_gaps.proposal: Customer-approved package repositories/mirrors with provenance, compatibility metadata, checksums and vendor-signature verification where supported; use prior printer research for exact update rights.
acceptance_criteria: A package for the wrong product/region/branch is rejected.
Offline import preserves source/release metadata and never invents an undocumented vendor upload API.
No campaign is advertised until exact vendor-driver update/recovery qualification exists.

integration_gaps.title: Optional broker/automation-platform bridges
integration_gaps.proposal: Use versioned webhooks/collector bridges for customer automation first; introduce a native broker transport only for demonstrated throughput/topology requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge delivery and consumer dedup semantics are documented.
A broker outage is bounded by the durable queue policy.
No mandatory message-bus dependency is introduced into the single-site installation without a justified need.
